text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

Service quality improvement by Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), Poland's telecom monopolist, will prove impossible without opening the market to competition, Consumer and Competition Protection Office President Andrzej Sopocko said.

- Privatisations of telecom companies carried out globally show that the Polish TPSA telecom firm should be privatised in several stages through a public offer, HSBC Investment Services President Hubert A. Janiszewski said.
- By year-end Poland's unemployment rate, though falling, will be at 13.5 percent, among the highest in Europe, Poland's planning ministry said.
September was the seventh month running in which the number of unemployed fell.
- After a break of 13 years the ZA Kedzierzyn artificial fertilizer maker in southwestern Poland has reintroduced river barge shipments of its products addressed to buyers in Germany and Holland.
The decision followed delays caused by reloading bottlenecksks in the northwestern port of Szczecin.
- Poland's industrial output declined in October, the Gdansk-based Market Economy Research Institute said.
Firms surveyed expected the trend to continue for the next few months.
- The Gdynia shipyard will deliver an 18,400 deadweight tonnage (DWT) container ship to Germany's Alpha Ship shipping company.
This year the shipyard will construct 10 ships, bringing it 945 million zlotys in revenues.
- The Tarnow-based Zaklady Azotowe SA artificial fertilizer maker has set up a PVC window assembly plant in Zabno, southern Poland, which cost the company 5.3 million zlotys.

- By November 10 this year Poland's sugar production exceeded one million tonnes. The country will produce up to 1.2 million more tonnes by year-end, sugar industry council President Artur Sugier said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Polish-made petrol fuels are sold in 150 petrol stations owned or licensed by Poland's refineries but are unavailable in 4,700 stations around the country.
- Around 200 km of roads in Poland are modernised every year, mainly through the modernisation programme assisted by the World Bank, Public Roads director general Tadeusz Suwara said.
- The Kutno-based Nijhof Wassink truck dealer and forwarding firm was granted an International Standards Organisation (ISO) 9002 certificate for its service quality.

- The nationalist right-wing Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) will support the Business Alliance formed to promote small and medium-sized business interests, ROP leader Jan Olszewski said.
- The Sanok-based Autosan bus-maker will produce up to 60 Cezar luxury tourist buses constructed on Mercedes 404 chassis.
- The Dolna Odra electric power plant will invest around $70 million in desulphurisation equipment to neutralise up to 94 percent of its exhausts.
- Poland's meat processors are limiting meat purchases due to a decline in retail meat sales, the state agricultural production monotoring body PISPA said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Debica tyre company will deliver 1,400 wheels with tyres worth several hundred thousand dollars to the Sanok-based Autosan bus plant, Debica's marketing director Andrzej Stelmach said.
- During the current visit of the Polish foreign trade ministry delegation in Kuwait the two countries signed an agreement on avoiding double taxation.
- The World bank will lend money to the Lublin-based soft commodity exchange, the Bank's special envoy Richard Lacroix said.
ZYCIE
- The Warsaw-based bank PKO BP has introduced a new six- month consumer credit bearing 24.5 percent annual interest, the bank's spokeman Janusz Ostaszewski said.

- Poland's Consumer and Competition Protection Office suspects that genetically altered food has entered the Polish market and that consumers are not aware of it, the office's spokeswoman Jolanta Micel-Thor said.
